---
title: How to migrate from Pages to the App Router
nav_title: App Router
description: Learn how to upgrade your existing Next.js application from the Pages Router to the App Router.
---

This guide will help you:

- [Update your Next.js application from version 12 to version 13](#nextjs-version)
- [Upgrade features that work in both the `pages` and the `app` directories](#upgrading-new-features)
- [Incrementally migrate your existing application from `pages` to `app`](#migrating-from-pages-to-app)

## Upgrading

### Node.js Version

The minimum Node.js version is now **v18.17**. See the [Node.js documentation](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v18.x/api/) for more information.

### Next.js Version

My Page

00023| } 00024| ``` 00025| 00026| ## Good to know 00027| 00028| - The `.js`, `.jsx`, or `.tsx` file extensions can be used for `page`. 00029| - A `page` is always the **leaf** of the route subtree. 00030| - A `page` file is required to make a route segment **publicly accessible**. 00031| - Pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components) by default, but can be set to a [Client Component](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client). 00032| - In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `page.js` is the innermost file convention. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 00066| 00067| #### `searchParams` (optional) 00068| 00069| A promise that resolves to an object containing the [search parameters](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Learn/Common_questions/What_is_a_URL#parameters) of the current URL. For example: 00070| 00071| ```tsx filename="app/shop/page.tsx" switcher 00072| export default async function Page({ 00073| searchParams, 00074| }: { 00075| searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }> 00076| }) { 00077| const filters = (await searchParams).filters 00078| } 00079| ``` 00080| 00081| ```jsx filename="app/shop/page.js" switcher 00082| export default async function Page({ searchParams }) { 00083| const filters = (await searchParams).filters 00084| } 00085| ``` 00086| 00087| Client Component **pages** can also access `searchParams` using React’s [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) hook: 00088| 00089| ```tsx filename="app/shop/page.tsx" switcher 00090| 'use client' 00091| import { use } from 'react' 00092| 00093| export default function Page({ 00094| searchParams, 00095| }: { 00096| searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }> 00097| }) { 00098| const filters = use(searchParams).filters 00099| } 00100| ``` 00101| 00102| ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher 00103| 'use client' 00104| import { use } from 'react' 00105| 00106| export default function Page({ searchParams }) { 00107| const filters = use(searchParams).filters 00108| } 00109| ``` 00110| 00111| | Example URL | `searchParams` | 00112| | --------------- | ----------------------------- | 00113| | `/shop?a=1` | `Promise<{ a: '1' }>` | 00114| | `/shop?a=1&b=2` | `Promise<{ a: '1', b: '2' }>` | 00115| | `/shop?a=1&a=2` | `Promise<{ a: ['1', '2'] }>` | 00116| 00117| - Since the `searchParams` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values. 00118| - In version 14 and earlier, `searchParams` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 00119| - `searchParams` is a **[Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis)** whose values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it will opt the page into **[dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering)** at request time. 00120| - With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), where you access `searchParams` in the component tree determines how much of the page can be prerendered. See [Maximizing the static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#maximizing-the-static-shell). 00121| - `searchParams` is a plain JavaScript object, not a `URLSearchParams` instance. 00122| 00123| ### Page Props Helper 00124| 00125| You can type pages with `PageProps` to get strongly typed `params` and `searchParams` from the route literal. `PageProps` is a globally available helper. 00126| 00127| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" 00128| export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { 00129| const { slug } = await props.params 00130| const query = await props.searchParams 00131| return

00132| } 00133| ``` 00134| 00135| > **Good to know** 00136| > 00137| > - Using a literal route (e.g. `'/blog/[slug]'`) enables autocomplete and strict keys for `params`. 00138| > - Static routes resolve `params` to `{}`. 00139| > - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build`, or with `next typegen`. 00140| > - After type generation, the `PageProps` helper is globally available. 00156| } 00157| ``` 00158| 00159| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 00160| export default async function Page({ params }) { 00161| const { slug } = await params 00162| return

00163| } 00164| ``` 00165| 00166| ### Handling filtering with `searchParams` 00167| 00168| You can use the `searchParams` prop to handle filtering, pagination, or sorting based on the query string of the URL. 00169| 00170| ```tsx filename="app/shop/page.tsx" switcher 00171| export default async function Page({ 00172| searchParams, 00173| }: { 00174| searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }> 00175| }) { 00176| const { page = '1', sort = 'asc', query = '' } = await searchParams 00177| 00178| return ( 00179|

00184|
00185| ) 00186| } 00187| ``` 00188| 00189| ```jsx filename="app/shop/page.js" switcher 00190| export default async function Page({ searchParams }) { 00191| const { page = '1', sort = 'asc', query = '' } = await searchParams 00192| 00193| return ( 00194|

00003| description: API reference for the layout.js file.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| The `layout` file is used to define a layout in your Next.js application.
00007| 
00008| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher
00009| export default function DashboardLayout({
00010|   children,
00011| }: {
00012|   children: React.ReactNode
00013| }) {
00014|   return <section>{children}</section>
00015| }
00016| ```
00017| 
00018| ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher
00019| export default function DashboardLayout({ children }) {
00020|   return <section>{children}</section>
00021| }
00022| ```
00023| 
00024| In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `layout.js` is the outermost component in a route segment. It wraps `template.js`, `error.js`, `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, and `page.js`.
00025| 
00026| A **root layout** is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. It is used to define the `<html>` and `<body>` tags and other globally shared UI.
00027| 
00028| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00029| export default function RootLayout({
00030|   children,
00031| }: {
00032|   children: React.ReactNode
00033| }) {
00034|   return (
00035|     <html lang="en">
00036|       <body>{children}</body>
00037|     </html>
00038|   )
00039| }
00040| ```
00041| 
00042| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00043| export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
00044|   return (
00045|     <html lang="en">
00046|       <body>{children}</body>
00047|     </html>
00048|   )
00049| }
00050| ```
00051| 
00052| ## Reference
00053| 
00054| ### Props
00055| 
00056| #### `children` (required)
00057| 
00058| Layout components should accept and use a `children` prop. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable.
00059| 
00060| #### `params` (optional)
00061| 
00062| A promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to that layout.
00063| 
00064| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.tsx" switcher
00065| export default async function Layout({
00066|   children,
00067|   params,
00068| }: {
00069|   children: React.ReactNode
00070|   params: Promise<{ team: string }>
00071| }) {
00072|   const { team } = await params
00073| }
00074| ```
00075| 
00076| ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js" switcher
00077| export default async function Layout({ children, params }) {
00078|   const { team } = await params
00079| }
00080| ```
00081|

00083| | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
00084| | `app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |
00085| | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/layout.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |
00086| | `app/blog/[...slug]/layout.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`    |
00087| 
00088| - Since the `params` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values.
00089|   - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.

---
title: dynamicParams
description: API reference for the dynamicParams route segment config option.
---

The `dynamicParams` option allows you to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with [generateStaticParams](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params).

```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
export const dynamicParams = true // true | false
```

```js filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
export const dynamicParams = true // true | false
```

- **`true`** (default): Dynamic route segments not included in `generateStaticParams` are generated at request time.
- **`false`**: Dynamic route segments not included in `generateStaticParams` will return a 404.

> **Good to know**:
>
> - This option replaces the `fallback: true | false | blocking` option of `getStaticPaths` in the `pages` directory.
> - `dynamicParams` is not available when [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.

title: dynamicParams
description: API reference for the dynamicParams route segment config option.
---

The `dynamicParams` option allows you to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with [generateStaticParams](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params).

```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
export const dynamicParams = true // true | false
```

```js filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
export const dynamicParams = true // true | false
```

- **`true`** (default): Dynamic route segments not included in `generateStaticParams` are generated at request time.
- **`false`**: Dynamic route segments not included in `generateStaticParams` will return a 404.

> **Good to know**:
>
> - This option replaces the `fallback: true | false | blocking` option of `getStaticPaths` in the `pages` directory.
> - `dynamicParams` is not available when [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.

If [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) are detected on the route, Next.js will fetch the resource on every request.
53:- **`no-store`**: Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server on every request, even if Request-time APIs are not detected on the route.
54:- **`force-cache`**: Next.js looks for a matching request in its server-side cache. A request matches on its URL, method, headers, and body, so requests that differ in any of these are cached separately.
58:> **Good to know**: Caching is opt-in. Set `cache: 'force-cache'` to cache any request, including `POST` and requests that send `authorization` or `cookie` headers. [Draft Mode](/docs/app/guides/draft-mode) bypasses the cache entirely (no read or write).
74:> - If an individual `fetch()` request sets a `revalidate` number lower than the [default `revalidate`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#route-segment-config-revalidate) of a route, the whole route revalidation interval will be decreased.
76:> - Conflicting options such as `{ revalidate: 3600, cache: 'no-store' }` are not allowed, both will be ignored, and in development mode a warning will be printed to the terminal.
101:### Fetch default `auto no store` and `cache: 'no-store'` not showing fresh data in development

This means uncached requests will not show fresh data between HMR refreshes. However, the cache will be cleared on navigation or full-page reloads.

events.content:
Migration complete. All routes verified working (200s, 404, API CRUD, dynamic metadata), build passes, typecheck passes, `pages/` deleted.

**What changed (per this Next 16 canary's docs):**

- `_app.js` + `_document.js` → `app/layout.tsx` — root layout with `<html>`/`<body>`, header/nav/footer, globals.css, `next/font/google` Inter (replaces the font `<link>`), and `metadata` for description/favicon
- `getServerSideProps` (`pages/index.js`) → async Server Component `app/page.tsx` using `await headers()` + `fetch(..., { cache: 'no-store' })`
- `getStaticProps`/`revalidate: 60` (`pages/blog`) → `app/blog/page.tsx` with `export const revalidate = 60` + `next: { revalidate: 60 }` fetch
- `getStaticPaths`/`fallback: 'blocking'` (`pages/blog/[id]`) → `generateStaticParams()` + `export const dynamicParams = true`; `router.isFallback` removed; `params` is now a `Promise` and awaited; metadata via `generateMetadata`; fetch failure → `notFound()`
- `next/head` → `metadata` / `generateMetadata` exports (incl. `openGraph`)
- `pages/api/*` → Route Handlers `app/api/posts/route.ts` (GET/POST) and `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts` (GET/PUT/DELETE) using Web `Request`/`Response.json()`; 405 handling is now automatic
- `pages/404.js` → `app/not-found.tsx`; `pages/_error.js` (`getInitialProps`) → `app/error.tsx` + `app/global-error.tsx` client boundaries using the new `retry()` prop
- `useRouter` from `next/router` → `useRouter` from `next/navigation` in client components (`NavigateButton`, `BackButton`); plain `<a href>` internal links upgraded to `<Link>`
- `AppProvider` moved to a typed `'use client'` component; all files converted to TypeScript (`Post`/`Comment` types in `lib/types.ts`)
